8:
SAY:
- "Today we need a pencil, a mini whiteboard with a texta, and our booklet."
- "Have your celebration drawings ready for the class presentation."

DO:
- Hold up each item.
- Wait until each student has them ready.
- Confirm students have their celebration drawings from previous lessons.

TEACHER NOTES:
Quick setup. Make sure every student has their full set of drawings (opening sentence, detail sentences, final sentence) ready.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who lost a drawing. Help them quickly redraw a simple version.
9:
TEACHER NOTES:
Section divider for vocabulary. The focus word is 'ferocious'. Move on to the routine slide.
10:
SOURCES:
Collins Primary School Dictionary, https://schools.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/primary, accessed 11.2.26

SAY:
- "Our word today is ferocious."
- "Say it with me. Ferocious."
- "If something is ferocious, it is violent and fierce."
- "In the story, the dragon is described as having a ferocious face."
- "Sailors have to navigate ferocious storms. A tiger is ferocious when hunting."

DO:
- Point to the word.
- Have students choral say it three times. The word has three syllables, so model fe-ro-cious.
- Make a fierce face when you say it.

TEACHER NOTES:
The word is long for Foundation. Use the fierce face action. Foundation students may not know 'violent' or 'fierce'. Briefly define 'fierce' as 'wild and strong'.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who can repeat the word but not the meaning. Use the fierce face action.
11:
SAY:
- "In Fang Fang's Chinese New Year, the dragon is described as having a ferocious face."
- "That tells us the dragon does not look calm or friendly."
- "It probably has sharp teeth showing and angry eyes."
- "Show me your ferocious face."

DO:
- Read the slide aloud.
- Cue students to make a ferocious face.
- Connect to the dragon picture from the read aloud.

TEACHER NOTES:
Unpacks the meaning through the story example. Foundation students need the action (face) to anchor the word.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who confuse 'ferocious' with 'fearful'. Show that ferocious means scary, not scared.
12:
SAY:
- "Is this ferocious?"
- "Ask: a lion roaring loudly? Expected: yes."
- "Ask: a kitten purring? Expected: no."
- "Show me thumbs up for ferocious, thumbs down for not ferocious."

DO:
- Take one example at a time.
- Cue thumbs after each.
- Mime each animal as you say it.

TEACHER NOTES:
Quick check. The contrast between lion and kitten is clear for Foundation.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who think any animal is ferocious. Use the kitten example to push back.
13:
SAY:
- "Complete the sentence: The storm was ferocious because..."
- "Listen to the example: The storm was ferocious because the thunder crashed and the wind roared through the trees."
- "Tell your partner why a storm could be ferocious."

DO:
- Read the example aloud.
- Take a partner share.
- Take 1 to 2 responses.
- Affirm sensible reasons.

TEACHER NOTES:
This slide builds oral language using 'ferocious'. Foundation students may need the example before they try.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who freeze. Prompt 'what does a strong storm sound like?'
14:
SAY:
- "Complete the sentence: If something is described as ferocious, it is wild and blank."
- "Ask: fierce or calm? Expected: fierce."
- "Show me on your fingers, one for fierce, two for calm."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal.
- Have students choral say 'ferocious means wild and fierce'.

CFU CHECKPOINT:
Technique: Show Me Fingers
Script:
- Ask: which word completes the sentence, fierce or calm? Expected: fierce.
- Scan for: most fingers showing 1.
PROCEED:
- >=80% show 1. Move on to recount work.
PIVOT:
- Most likely: students confuse 'wild' with 'calm'.
- Reteach: do the fierce face and the calm face. Show the difference.
- Re-check: ask 'is a calm pond ferocious?' Expected: no.

TEACHER NOTES:
Threshold check for vocabulary.

WATCH FOR:
- Students with mixed fingers. Take one of each and ask 'why?'
15:
TEACHER NOTES:
Section divider for understanding, responding to and creating text. The next slides build the oral presentation of the celebration recount.
16:
SAY:
- "Let's look at the structure of a recount."
- "Opening sentence: On my last birthday, my family and I went to the beach."
- "Detail sentences: First..., Then..., After that..."
- "Final sentence: It made me feel special because I spent time with my family at my favourite place."
- "Show me the icon action for each part."

DO:
- Read each part aloud.
- Use the matching icon action (when, where, who, events, feeling).
- Have students do the actions with you.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: revise the structure of a recount using the modelled birthday example. Students do the actions for each icon. This is the I Do for the presentation focus.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who freeze on actions. Pair with a confident neighbour.
17:
SAY:
- "When we present, we need to follow some key steps."
- "One: stand up tall."
- "Two: face the audience."
- "Three: hold your picture."
- "Four: speak in a big, clear voice."

DO:
- Read each step aloud.
- Model each step yourself.
- Have students stand up and try each one.

TEACHER NOTES:
Key teaching for presentation skills. Foundation students need explicit modelling of each step. Keep it short and active.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who slouch or look down. Stand near them and gently remind.
18:
SAY:
- "Listen to my recount."
- "On my last birthday, my family and I went to the beach."
- "First, I played cricket with my family on the sand."
- "Then, my brother and I went swimming in the ocean."
- "After that, we shared and ate lots of yummy food."
- "It made me feel special because I spent time with my family at my favourite place."
- "Ask: what good things did you notice?"

DO:
- Stand up tall.
- Face the class.
- Hold up a picture.
- Speak with a clear voice.
- Take 2 to 3 student responses.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: model the presentation. As you say the recount, ask students to notice positive things about how you present.

WATCH FOR:
- Students fidgeting. Cue them with 'remember to look at me'.
19:
SAY:
- "What good things did you notice about my presentation?"
- "Ask: looking at the audience, using the picture, ending with the final sentence, speaking clearly?"
- "Tell your partner one thing you noticed."

DO:
- Read the slide bullets aloud.
- Pair share.
- Take 2 to 3 responses.
- Affirm each observation.

TEACHER NOTES:
We Do reflection. Foundation students may struggle to articulate what they noticed. Use the slide bullets as a scaffold.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who freeze. Prompt 'did I look at you or at the floor?'
20:
SAY:
- "Are these good things to do when presenting?"
- "Ask: staring at your shoes? Expected: no."
- "Ask: looking at the audience? Expected: yes."
- "Ask: mumbling quietly? Expected: no."
- "Ask: speaking in a loud, clear voice? Expected: yes."
- "Show me thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no."

DO:
- Take one example at a time.
- Cue thumbs after each.
- Mime each behaviour for fun.
- Existing note: model each one with the sentence 'Then, my brother and I went swimming in the ocean'.

CFU CHECKPOINT:
Technique: Thumbs Up, Thumbs Down
Script:
- Ask each behaviour in turn. Expected answers: no, yes, no, yes.
- Scan for: matching thumbs.
PROCEED:
- >=80% match on most. Move to partner practice.
PIVOT:
- Most likely: students think mumbling is okay because they are shy.
- Reteach: model loud and clear, then mumble. Compare the two.
- Re-check: ask 'which one helps the audience hear you?' Expected: loud and clear.

TEACHER NOTES:
Threshold check before partner practice.

WATCH FOR:
- Students with mixed thumbs. Take one of each and ask 'why?'
21:
SAY:
- "Now you will practise your recount with a partner."
- "Use the checklist."
- "Stand up tall. Face the audience. Look at the audience. Hold your picture. Speak in a clear, loud voice."
- "Take turns."

DO:
- Pair students up.
- Listen in to a few pairs.
- Praise students who follow the checklist.
- Coach students who slouch or mumble.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: students practise presenting with their drawings. This is the rehearsal before the class presentation.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who whisper. Stand near them and model loud-but-not-shouty.
22:
SAY:
- "Now we will share our recounts with the class."
- "When you listen, think of a star: something you liked about the recount or presentation."
- "When it is your turn, stand up tall, face the audience, hold your picture, and speak clearly."

DO:
- Invite each student to present their recount.
- Hold or point to the pictorial representation.
- After each presentation, invite one positive star comment from the class.
- Keep the tone warm and supportive.

ENABLING & EXTENDING:
ENABLING PROMPT:
- Task: Provide a visual checklist (eyes for 'look at the audience', a microphone for 'speak clearly'). Stand near the student.
EXTENDING PROMPT:
- Task: Confident students can present their picture to a small group during the gallery walk.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: invite students to present, audience listens respectfully, one positive star after each. This is the formal You Do.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who freeze on the spot. Stand beside them and read a sentence with them.
- Audience members not listening. Re-cue with 'we are giving stars'.
23:
SAY:
- "Now we will do a gallery walk."
- "Walk around the room and look at each other's recount drawings."
- "Ask: are any similar to yours? How are they different?"
- "You can also present your picture to a small group."

DO:
- Display the drawings around the room.
- Cue students to walk and look.
- Listen to small group sharing.
- Bring students back together when finished.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: gallery walk to view each other's work. This is a calm closing to the recount unit.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who rush past pictures. Slow them down with 'find one celebration that is different from yours'.
24:
TEACHER NOTES:
Section divider for sentence-level writing. The focus is orally expanding sentences with adjectives. This is the final adjective practice in the unit.
25:
SAY:
- "Remember, an adjective is a word that tells us more about a noun."
- "Adjectives can tell us about size, colour, shape, age, or quality."

DO:
- Read the slide aloud.
- Use the paint brush action.
- Have students choral repeat 'adjective tells us more about a noun'.

TEACHER NOTES:
Quick I Do revision before sorting practice.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who can repeat but not apply. The next slides will check.
26:
SAY:
- "Is this word an adjective?"
- "Ask: loud? Expected: yes, it is an adjective."
- "Show me thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal with thumbs.
- Connect 'loud' to the firecrackers in the read aloud.

TEACHER NOTES:
First sort question. Foundation students will use thumbs to sort each word as an adjective or not. The slide also shows 'bright' (adjective) and 'birds' (not) as anchor examples.

WATCH FOR:
- Students with mixed thumbs. Ask 'does loud tell us more about a noun?'
27:
SAY:
- "Is this word an adjective?"
- "Ask: dragon? Expected: no, it is a noun."
- "Show me thumbs up or thumbs down."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal with thumbs.
- Remind students that 'dragon' is a thing, so it is a noun.

TEACHER NOTES:
Second sort question. The contrast between 'loud' (adjective) and 'dragon' (noun) helps students see the difference.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who say yes for everything. Use the test 'can you point to it?'
28:
SAY:
- "Is this word an adjective?"
- "Ask: bright? Expected: yes, it is an adjective."
- "Show me thumbs up or thumbs down."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal with thumbs.
- Connect 'bright' to the dragon or fireworks.

TEACHER NOTES:
Third sort question.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who copy a friend. Ask them why.
29:
SAY:
- "Is this word an adjective?"
- "Ask: fireworks? Expected: no, it is a noun."
- "Show me thumbs up or thumbs down."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal with thumbs.
- Remind students that 'fireworks' are things, so it is a noun.

TEACHER NOTES:
Fourth sort question.

WATCH FOR:
- Students confused by 'fireworks' being plural. The test is 'can you point to a thing?'
30:
SAY:
- "Is this word an adjective?"
- "Ask: red? Expected: yes, it is an adjective."
- "Show me thumbs up or thumbs down."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal with thumbs.
- Use the paint brush action.

TEACHER NOTES:
Fifth sort question. Colours are easy adjectives to remember.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who say 'red' is a thing. Show that 'red' describes a thing.
31:
SAY:
- "Is this word an adjective?"
- "Ask: lantern? Expected: no, it is a noun."
- "Show me thumbs up or thumbs down."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal with thumbs.
- Remind students that 'lantern' is a thing.

TEACHER NOTES:
Sixth sort question.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who confuse 'lantern' with the colours of a lantern. Use the test.
32:
SAY:
- "Is this word an adjective?"
- "Ask: noodles? Expected: no, it is a noun."
- "Show me thumbs up or thumbs down."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal with thumbs.
- Remind students that 'noodles' are things.

TEACHER NOTES:
Seventh sort question.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who say yes because food can describe things. Use the test.
33:
SAY:
- "Is this word an adjective?"
- "Ask: tasty? Expected: yes, it is an adjective."
- "Show me thumbs up or thumbs down."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal with thumbs.
- Use 'tasty' in a phrase like 'tasty noodles'.

TEACHER NOTES:
Eighth sort question. The phrase 'tasty noodles' shows the adjective in action.

WATCH FOR:
- Students confused. Show that 'tasty' describes the noodles.
34:
SAY:
- "Is this word an adjective?"
- "Ask: colourful? Expected: yes, it is an adjective."
- "Show me thumbs up or thumbs down."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal with thumbs.
- Use 'colourful' in a phrase.

TEACHER NOTES:
Ninth sort question.

WATCH FOR:
- Students confused by 'colour' inside 'colourful'. Show the whole word means full of colour.
35:
SAY:
- "Is this word an adjective?"
- "Ask: envelope? Expected: no, it is a noun."
- "Show me thumbs up or thumbs down."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal with thumbs.
- Remind students that 'envelope' is a thing.

TEACHER NOTES:
Tenth and last sort question. After this comes the formal sort task.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who guess. Use the test 'can you point to it?'
36:
SAY:
- "Now we will sort all the words into two categories."
- "Adjectives go on one side. Not adjectives (nouns) go on the other side."
- "I will read each word. You tell me where it goes."

DO:
- Read each word in turn.
- Take a class response or thumb signal.
- Place each word in its category.
- Ask 'why?' for at least one word in each category.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: sort the cards into two groups and discuss why. Adjectives (loud, bright, red, colourful, tasty) describe. Nouns (dragon, lantern, fireworks, noodles, envelope, present) are things.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who put a noun with adjectives. Use the test.
- Confident sorters who can explain. Use them as peer coaches for slower students.
37:
SAY:
- "Listen to two sentences."
- "The lion danced."
- "The colourful lion danced."
- "Ask: which one helps the listener picture the lion best? Expected: the second one (with colourful)."
- "Show me on your fingers."

DO:
- Read both sentences aloud.
- Take responses on fingers.
- Reveal the answer.
- Read the expanded sentence again.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: think aloud as you choose an adjective. The slide options are brave, thin, colourful. Foundation students should choose the one that matches the picture.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who pick 'thin'. Push back: does the lion in the picture look thin?
38:
SAY:
- "There are often lots of adjectives we can use."
- "Each one makes the sentence sound a bit different."
- "For example: The colourful lion danced. The ferocious lion danced. The energetic lion danced."
- "Each one tells us something different about the lion."

DO:
- Read each example aloud.
- Have students choral repeat each one.
- Briefly explain 'energetic' as 'full of energy' for Foundation students.

TEACHER NOTES:
This I Do shows that adjectives can be swapped. Connect 'ferocious' to today's vocabulary word.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who think there is only one right adjective. Reassure them many can fit.
39:
SAY:
- "The dragon twists through the street."
- "Ask: what adjective could we add? Expected: playful, festive, bright, long."
- "Now: The playful dragon twists through the street."
- "Can you think of another adjective instead of playful?"

DO:
- Read the original sentence.
- Take adjective ideas from students.
- Read the expanded sentence with one chosen adjective.
- Try a second adjective so students hear the difference.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: work with students to choose an adjective that fits. Encourage trying more than one.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who repeat 'playful' every time. Push for variety.
40:
SAY:
- "Lisa tried the dumplings."
- "Ask: what adjective could we add? Expected: tasty, delicious, hot, steamed."
- "Now: Lisa tried the tasty dumplings."
- "Can you think of another adjective instead of tasty?"

DO:
- Read the original sentence.
- Take adjective ideas.
- Read the expanded sentence with one chosen adjective.
- Try a second adjective.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: work with students. Connect to Lisa eating in the read aloud.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who suggest 'lumpy' or 'cold'. Affirm but redirect to ones that match the picture.
41:
SAY:
- "They looked at the eels."
- "Ask: what adjective could we add? Expected: slippery, wriggly, long."
- "Now: They looked at the wriggly eels."
- "Can you think of another adjective instead of wriggly?"

DO:
- Read the original sentence.
- Take adjective ideas.
- Read the expanded sentence.
- Try a second adjective.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: work with students. The slide also shows 'tall' and 'cold' as options - 'tall' does not fit eels.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who pick 'tall'. Push back: are eels tall?
42:
SAY:
- "Which adjective would NOT make sense in this sentence?"
- "The fireworks exploded."
- "Ask: sparkly, colourful, or quiet? Expected: quiet."
- "Show me on your fingers."

DO:
- Cover the answer.
- Reveal.
- Have students choral say 'fireworks are not quiet'.

CFU CHECKPOINT:
Technique: Show Me Fingers
Script:
- Ask: which adjective does NOT make sense, sparkly, colourful, or quiet? Expected: quiet.
- Scan for: most fingers showing 3.
PROCEED:
- >=80% show 3. Move to the You Do.
PIVOT:
- Most likely: students confused by the negative question.
- Reteach: read each adjective with 'fireworks'. Listen to which one sounds wrong.
- Re-check: ask 'are fireworks quiet?' Expected: no.

TEACHER NOTES:
Threshold check. Foundation students may find 'NOT' tricky. Slow down and read each option clearly.

WATCH FOR:
- Students with mixed fingers. Take one of each and ask 'why?'
43:
SAY:
- "With your partner, take turns expanding a sentence using an adjective."
- "Choose a noun card, then choose an adjective card to describe it."
- "Once you have both, say the sentence."
- "Take turns until you have done four to six sentences."

DO:
- Provide noun cards and adjective cards to each pair.
- Set them off.
- Listen in.
- Invite a few students to share one expanded sentence.

ENABLING & EXTENDING:
ENABLING PROMPT:
- Task: Pre-match the nouns to adjectives so students just construct the sentence.
EXTENDING PROMPT:
- Task: Choose two adjectives that could describe the same noun. Explain how each creates a different picture.

TEACHER NOTES:
Existing note: students repeat with several cards. This is the You Do for the unit's adjective work.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who freeze on the cards. Pre-match for them.
- Confident students. Push them to the extension.
44:
SAY:
- "Here are some sentence kernels you can use."
- "The dragon made a roar. The fireworks exploded. The lantern glowed. They ate the noodles. They handed out envelopes."
- "Pick one and add an adjective."

DO:
- Read each kernel aloud.
- Have students choose one with their partner.
- Listen in.

TEACHER NOTES:
Kernel sentences for the partner activity. Each connects to the read aloud or the unit. Foundation students can pick one and try.

WATCH FOR:
- Students who only pick one kernel. Push them to try a second.
45:
TEACHER NOTES:
Closing credits slide. End of the unit. Save students' celebration drawings if they go home or into a class display.
